_about: code2zfl base catalog for PHP. DATA, not code: what counts as an attacker-controlled SOURCE, what is a SINK (and in which context), and which functions SUBSTITUTE a value by a verified one for a context (E40: no function launders a mark; the only sanitizer is substitution). A row here is a claim about PHP, and `measured` says whether the fixtures exercise it.

_notes.inert_guards: READ, AND FOUND WANTING. A guard we cannot read makes the value Z (the checker is named, verdict OPEN). These we CAN read, and what they answer confines nothing about the value: file_exists() says a path is on disk — an attacker's upload, a log, /etc/passwd are all on disk, and it is not the set the developer named at this site; is_string()/is_array() fix the type and forbid no quote; count()/strlen() measure. So they are treated as no guard at all, and a verdict on the value stands. NOT here, deliberately: class_exists / function_exists / method_exists / is_callable / str_starts_with / str_contains — each of those CAN confine (a prefix check is a real path confinement), and they stay unknown-Z until read case by case. MEASURED on SMF 2026-09-09: file_exists 252, is_array 112, is_file 67, is_dir 36, is_string 29 OPEN verdicts carried one of these as a named cause.
_notes.addslashes: listed as TRANSPARENT on purpose: a string transformation, not a substitution by a verified element; bypassable (multibyte). Taint passes, sanitization is NOT credited.
_notes.strip_tags: transparent for the same reason: it is not an HTML escaper.
_notes.transparent: taint passes through; any sanitization already earned is DROPPED (substr of an escaped string can end in a lone backslash; stripslashes undoes escaping outright). Too strict is a verdict that can be redeemed; too lax is one that lies.
_notes.preserving: taint passes through and earned sanitization is KEPT: case changes, whitespace trimming and padding cannot create a quote or strand a backslash — after mysqli_real_escape_string no raw whitespace-escape remains to strip. ARGUED from the escaper's contract, not measured against MySQL; a counterexample moves the entry to `transparent`.
_notes._SERVER: attacker-written entries only: HTTP_* (every request header, HTTP_HOST and HTTP_X_FORWARDED_FOR included), the request line and path. REMOTE_ADDR, SERVER_*, DOCUMENT_ROOT are set by the server and read as constants. A computed key is assumed hot.
_notes.narrowing: taint passes; only a NUMERIC substitution survives (digits stay digits under any cut), a context escape does not (substr can strand a backslash).
_notes.explode/implode: preserving when the delimiter is a literal without quote, backslash or NUL (it cannot strand an escape); otherwise narrowing.
_notes.header/callable: added 2026-09-08 after Psalm reported a TaintedHeader (header('Location: '.$url)) and a TaintedCallable (new $classname) our catalog had no sink for. `callable` fires on new $x(), $x(), $obj->$m() and call_user_func*; the judged value is the NAME, not the arguments.
_notes.guards: a condition is an ACT OF CHECKING: inside the branch it protects, the checked value is substituted (E40 — membership in a fixed set is a substitution). Credited only when the set/pattern is fixed: in_array against a literal array, ctype_*/is_numeric, an anchored regex over a plain character class, $x === 'literal', a literal switch case. After `if (!guard) exit/return;` the guard holds for what follows. `file_exists` is NOT a guard (traversal passes it).
_notes.unknown-call: an UNKNOWN call's result is Z even over constant arguments (2026-09-09): `$obj->get()` reads object state, `time()` reads the clock, file_get_contents('php://input') reads the request. What is NOT attacker-controlled is said here, as an ALLOW-LIST measured on real trees (transparent: path/time/random/version helpers; narrowing: array element extraction), never assumed.
_notes.html-subcontexts: 2026-09-09: the html sink has SUB-CONTEXTS read by a lexer over the output stream (atoms.php Html): body text and double-quoted attributes take `html`; a single-quoted attribute needs `html-sq` (htmlspecialchars/htmlentities with ENT_QUOTES — the default since PHP 8.1, so `--php 7.4` matters; FILTER_SANITIZE_*SPECIAL_CHARS always); an escaper whose flags carry quote bits of ZERO (ENT_NOQUOTES, or a bare doctype flag such as ENT_XML1/ENT_HTML5/ENT_HTML401) encodes NEITHER quote and takes `html-text` — body text only, no attribute at all (measured on PHP 8.3.6, 2026-09-10); a URL attribute needs `header` (URL-encoding); an unquoted attribute, a tag or attribute name, an event handler, style, <script>, <style>, a comment take only `*`. An output whose position cannot be read no longer counts as body text (2026-09-10): a substitution that covers EVERY position (`*`, or html with html-sq) still earns, anything narrower goes OPEN with the unread position named — an unread position is not the friendliest position.
_notes.header/setcookie: setcookie($name, $value, ...) carries the attacker-controlled part in the SECOND argument; judging the first (a constant name) returned EARNED on a live flaw. Found 2026-09-09 on bWAPP by Psalm's TaintedCookie, read in the source (xss_stored_2.php:29→36).
_notes.fixed-alphabet-encoders: base64_encode ([A-Za-z0-9+/=]) and bin2hex ([0-9a-f]) confine their output to a fixed alphabet with no quote, space, dot or bracket: a substitution for every context, like md5. str_replace/strtr with literal arguments whose replacement characters lie in [A-Za-z0-9_-,] keep such a substitution (strtr(base64_encode($x), '+/=', '-_,') in the blog engine, 2026-09-09).
